title: Sourcing & Contract Ops Intake
next_steps: Redwood to upload redlined MSA draft to shared drive by 2025-03-25
Customer to complete vendor risk questionnaire and return by 2025-03-28
Schedule follow-up pricing approval sync with procurement on 2025-04-01
action_items: Maya Chen: upload redlined MSA and annotated DPA (due 2025-03-25)
Liam O'Connor: confirm contract signatory details and legal exceptions list (due 2025-03-28)
Diego Ramos: produce SLA latency and availability addendum and sample monitoring dashboard screenshots (due 2025-03-27)
Sara Bloom: send completed security questionnaire and confirm SOC2 report access (due 2025-03-28)
header:
Date: 2025-03-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (NovaScale Procurement), Liam O'Connor (NovaScale Legal), Sara Bloom (NovaScale Security)
summary: Intake call between Redwood (AE+SE) and NovaScale procurement/legal/security to map contract gating, MSA/DPA exceptions, SLA requirements, and procurement approval timeline. Agreement to exchange redlines, complete vendor questionnaire, and return pricing/PO path by end of month.
topics: DPA / data residency and KMS requirements
SLA uptime, credits, and monitoring hooks
Procurement approval flow and PO/billing entity
questions: Can Redwood support per-tenant data residency in AWS eu-west-1?
What is Redwood's SLA and how are credits calculated?
Do you provide SOC2 Type II report and pen test summary?
How does billing/PO invoicing work for dedicated capacity?
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the procurement and contract ops intake for NovaScale, make sure we understand the gating items and timeline.
[00:18] Priya Patel: thanks Maya. we're mainly focused on two things — the MSA exceptions our legal team flagged, and ensuring the billing flow aligns with our finance expectations. we need PO based invoicing and a single billing entity.
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: hi, yes, from legal side the MSA had three ask items: data residency clause, liability cap and indemnity tweaks, and a DPA alignment. we also want a clear SLA with credits spelled out.
[00:49] Diego Ramos: quick intro, i'm Diego on infra and SLAs — happy to dig into latency/availability numbers. rough question: are you expecting dedicated or hosted to start?
[00:58] Priya Patel: procurement prefers hosted to move faster but finance may ok a committed reserved plan if pricing is right. we want to avoid long lead times for purchasing though.
[01:10] Maya Chen: noted. On the MSA redlines, we can upload a redlined version tonight — we'll flag any standard exceptions. Liam, is a liability cap tweak your main pain?
[01:22] Liam O'Connor: it's one of them. Also we have DPA language requiring customer-managed KMS for keys in private deployments. we need to know if Redwood supports customer KMS and HSM options.
[01:36] Sara Bloom: and on security — SOC2 is must, pen test summary is helpful, plus we need audit log retention for 2 years, and SSO with SAML. Also can we get a list of sub-processors?
[01:50] Diego Ramos: yes, Redwood supports SSO/SAML and audit logs; sub-processor list can be shared, though some items are redacted. For KMS, in Private deployments we have options for customer-managed keys; for hosted we use envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS for Dedicated in some cases — we'll put the matrix in the doc.
[02:15] Priya Patel: great, put that in writing. finance also asked about invoice cadence and whether you accept Net30 and PO numbers.
[02:25] Maya Chen: we support Net30 and PO numbers; for Hosted customers we invoice monthly based on usage, for Dedicated there is a reserved monthly charge plus overage. we'll include sample invoices.
[02:36] Liam O'Connor: can you also confirm the SLA uptime percentage and the credit calc? we saw a one-line in the public page but need firm language for contract.
[02:48] Diego Ramos: our standard SLA is 99.5% for hosted with tiered credits: under 99.5% is X% credit, under 99% larger credit — i'll send a draft addendum. For Dedicated we can negotiate a higher SLA with SLO targets and monitoring hooks.
[03:05] Priya Patel: when you say credits, how is that paid — account credit vs cash?
[03:11] Maya Chen: usually account credit against future invoices; if you need cash remediation that's an enterprise exception and we'd need finance/legal signoff.
[03:19] Sara Bloom: we also need to know about data deletion timelines when the contract ends — retention windows and certifying deletion.
[03:26] Diego Ramos: yes, standard is 30 day soft delete, 90 day backend retention for backups — but for Private we can do customer-requested immediate purge and provide a deletion certificate. we'll capture that in the DPA.
[03:40] Liam O'Connor: any limitations on log export for audit? we need streaming of audit logs to our SIEM.
[03:46] Diego Ramos: audit logs can be exported to your S3 or delivered via webhook; there are rate limits but we'll document sample configs.
[03:57] Priya Patel: timeline wise, procurement needs the redline by next week to queue for the pricing committee. target: vendor committee on 2025-04-04.
[04:06] Maya Chen: ok, we'll aim to get redlines by 2025-03-25. Diego, you'll prepare the SLA addendum and monitoring screenshots?
[04:14] Diego Ramos: yep, SLA addendum, sample Grafana dashboards and token/cost breakdowns — i'll include per-route token cost examples.
[04:22] Liam O'Connor: one more legal quirk: our privacy team wants to ensure subprocessor flow-down in DPA — can you accept those clauses?
[04:31] Maya Chen: we can accept many standard flow-downs but some vendor-specific terms may need review; we'll highlight non-starters in the redline.
[04:40] Sara Bloom: procurement flagged integration with our internal VPC connector for Private deployment. is there an onboarding runbook?
[04:49] Diego Ramos: yes, onboarding runbook exists — we'll share the private deploy runbook and checklist (network pre-reqs, firewall rules, peering, certs). link: https://redwood.example.com/internal/runbooks/private-onboard (placeholder).
[05:05] Priya Patel: good. on pricing, we need to know if there's a committed spend discount structure for 12 month vs 36 month.
[05:14] Maya Chen: we have reserved capacity tiers and term discounts; i'll put a couple scenarios into a spreadsheet and share.
[05:22] Liam O'Connor: also curious about indemnity language — our counsel often asks for mutual indemnities for data breaches.
[05:29] Maya Chen: understood. we'll mark that and propose Redwood's standard reciprocal indemnity language.
[05:36] Priya Patel: procurement also needs to know escalation contact and SLA warm handoff for production incidents.
[05:43] Diego Ramos: we'll include escalation matrices: support tiers, oncall, and escalation paths. also runbooks for incident postmortems.
[05:55] [cross talk] Liam O'Connor: (muttering) okay, and then about export controls —
[06:00] Maya Chen: sorry can you repeat?
[06:02] Liam O'Connor: export controls for model outputs, just flagging that our compliance officer will ask.
[06:07] Diego Ramos: good flag — we have policy docs that cover export compliance and region restrictions, we'll point to them.
[06:15] Priya Patel: are there any prior procurement hiccups that customers hit — do you have an onboarding SLA?
[06:23] Diego Ramos: onboarding SLA is typically 14-30 days depending on deployment mode; Hosted is fastest, Dedicated/Private longer because of infra provisioning.
[06:33] Maya Chen: quick recap: Redwood will upload redlined MSA + annotated DPA by 3/25, Diego to share SLA addendum and sample dashboards by 3/27, NovaScale returns vendor questionnaire by 3/28, and procurement will queue committee for 4/4. any issues?
[06:50] Priya Patel: that all sounds good. one ask: can you include a sample PO/invoice so our finance sees line items?
[06:56] Maya Chen: yes, sample invoice included in next message.
[07:00] Liam O'Connor: also want to capture any security exceptions up front to avoid surprises later.
[07:06] Sara Bloom: we'll compile the list after we review the questionnaire.
[07:10] Maya Chen: perfect. i'll follow up with links and next steps. thanks everyone.
[07:14] [END OF TRANSCRIPT — remainder of call had small wrap up and scheduling notes]
